audit_2026_10_23: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-10-23) — run after Mecklenburg County's feed FAILED this same audit (see PROGRESS.md 2026-10-23 expansion entry). (1) Layer 'Building Permits' (City of Raleigh, ArcGIS item owner OpenData_ral, public access): 184,756 rows all-time, issueddate 2000-02-22 to 2026-10-22; layer editingInfo.dataLastEditDate 2026-10-23T11:06:46Z (same-day). (2) VOLUME STABILITY measured by year: 2020 4,857 / 2021 5,746 / 2022 5,870 / 2023 5,728 / 2024 5,583 / 2025 5,426 / 2026 YTD 4,577 (through Oct 22) — no collapse; months run 370-566 through 2025 and 419-533 in 2026 (Oct partial 269). (3) Item description (city's own): 'This dataset includes all pending and approved permits related to buildings, as well as non-construction inspections permits. This dataset does not include plumbing, electrical, mechanical, right of way, grading or other types of permits.' Update frequency: Daily. Window population is permits WITH an issueddate (pending applications carry none: 7,101 all-time). (4) Terms: the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo names the Open Raleigh Data Policy — reuse under that policy; figures attributed to the City of Raleigh.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Raleigh only. Other Wake County jurisdictions (Cary, Apex, and the county's other towns) publish their permits separately and are not in this feed; totals here are City of Raleigh totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one permitnum in the City of Raleigh's Building Permits layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issueddate >= 2025-10-23), measured 2026-10-23 on a full audit pull of the window's permit numbers: 5,486 rows = 5,486 distinct permitnum, 0 duplicates, 0 null permit numbers. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: originaladdress1, as published (mixed case in the source). ZIP from originalzip.
field_map.application_date: applieddate (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date).
field_map.category: permitclassmapped, the city's own mapped class: Residential (3,905 window permits) / Non-Residential (1,581) — the Seattle treatment. It agrees exactly with the permit-number prefix (BLDR- = Residential, BLDNR- = Non-Residential, measured 3,905/3,905 and 1,581/1,581).
field_map.contractor_rule: contractorcompanyname ONLY — the permit's published contractor company of record (present on 4,857 of 5,486 window permits; empty string carries as NULL). The pull's column list never requests the parcel-owner fields (parcelownername, parcelowneraddress1/2 — property-owner person names and addresses), nor the contractor's email, phone, license number, or address fields.
field_map.issue_date: issueddate (epoch ms, converted). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the city records an issue date.
field_map.permit_number: permitnum (BLDR-/BLDNR- prefixed; unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.status: statuscurrent, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses: Issued 3,208 / Complete 2,185 / Expired-Closed 76 / Stop Work Order 8 / On Hold 6 / In Review 2 / Active 1 — every window record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states (expired, on hold, stop work) stay in the population, as in Fort Worth's issued-proven set.
field_map.valuation: estprojectcost, stored and published as reported. Measured on the full window (2026-10-23): stated on 5,486 of 5,486 permits (0 null), 603 at $0, 0 at $1, 4,883 above $1; median $53,898 (median positive $78,337); window total $2,313,538,637.59. Stamp scan: only 13 values above $1M repeat at all (2-3 times each), and every repeated value checked is identical buildings in one development at sibling addresses with sequential permit numbers (e.g. $1,789,195.02 at 2050/2058/2066 Green Orchard Cir) — the Boston signature of identical per-building estimates, not a cross-project stamp; worst-case excess if every repeat were a restatement is about 2% of the total. The largest permit ($308,249,031.38, a hotel project at 615 S Salisbury St) appears exactly once (13.3% of the total — the Chicago flagship shape; its description prints alongside). VALUES PUBLISH; the DB window sum must reproduce the source-side total, and September 2026 must match the source exactly (491 permits / $136,253,042.53).

history_range: issueddate 2000-02-22 onward in the source (184,756 rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule). The layer also carries 4,774 Demolition-type records, but their issueddate ends in 2021 — none fall in the window, so no demolition page exists; building permits are the window's whole population (permittypemapped = Building on 5,486 of 5,486).
license: Open Raleigh Data Policy (named in the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo); attribution: City of Raleigh, North Carolina
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 2,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: City of Raleigh open data — Building Permits
terms_status: verified-open-2026-10-23: the ArcGIS item record for 'Building Permits' (publisher: City of Raleigh open data, owner OpenData_ral; access public) names the Open Raleigh Data Policy in its licenseInfo — reuse permitted under that policy's conditions; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Raleigh' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Daily per the item description; MEASURED 2026-10-23: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-10-23T11:06:46Z (same day as the audit) and newest issueddate 2026-10-22. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 96h threshold.
watermark_field: issueddate + permitnum — refresh re-pulls by the issueddate watermark and upserts; permits whose status changes in place after issuance update on the monthly reconciliation pattern used by the other ArcGIS county (Fort Worth).
